text: Now we actually build Dana's requisition for fifty pump bearings. Let's walk every field that matters, in the order she'd fill it out, and see what Oracle Fusion does with each one.

When Dana starts a new requisition, several header fields default automatically: her name as preparer and requester, her requisitioning business unit, and her default deliver-to location. None of that is arbitrary - it's the same business unit setup from lesson three showing up as working defaults.

Dana searches the catalog for pump bearing and finds the PB-4400, already loaded with description, category, and price. She sets the quantity to fifty, and the line's estimated amount calculates automatically. She doesn't have to know or guess what Meridian charges.

A few fields matter well beyond this lesson. The need-by date becomes the expected delivery date on the purchase order. The deliver-to location drives where Priya will receive the shipment in chapter four. And the item and category drive which approval rules apply next lesson.

When Dana clicks submit, Oracle Fusion assigns a requisition number and routes it into approval - but nothing has actually been ordered yet. Meridian isn't involved until a purchase order exists. Up next, lesson seven: what happens while Dana's requisition waits for approval.
